 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet Cricket Australia's board has given its unanimous backing to Pat Cummins as Test captain © AFP Cricket Australia's board has given its unanimous backing to Pat Cummins as Test captain © AFP Cricket Australia's board has given its unanimous backing to Pat Cummins as Test captain, after a meeting called to address the renewed speculation over the 2018 tour of South Africa.
 CA chair David Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg met Cummins in Sydney on Friday. They discussed several issues including “his welfare, support required for the team and the forthcoming series against New Zealand” according to a board media release. The statement came after Josh Hazlewood said he would have to think about his own future in the side if Cummins was fired as Test captain.
 "We are absolutely determined to steward Australian Cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn," Boon said. "That's what the independent Forum we announced this week is about and the Board encourages all players and support staff to tell and discuss their stories there. We will be publishing the Terms of Reference in due course.
 "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa. We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised."
 Cummins said he would attend the forum, which CA set up this week for players and staff from the 2018 tour to give their accounts in private.
 "It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd on Friday. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly," Cummins said. "David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.
 "I support the Forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what's needed. Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority."
 The first of four Tests against New Zealand starts in Perth on December 9.
